summary: Public WebSocket rooms, one Durable Object per room name, that accept sockets with accept() and run a setInterval ping, so every room with a client connected is billed for duration the whole time.

also.contains: setInterval(() => this.broadcast(JSON.stringify({ type: "ping", at: Date.now() })), PING_MS);

expected_findings.explanation: Room accepts each socket with server.accept() instead of the Hibernation API and keeps a setInterval ping running, so the object cannot hibernate: it is billed for duration at 128 MB for as long as any client stays connected, about 461 GB-s per room per hour, and the timer keeps it in memory for up to 15 minutes after the last client leaves. Anyone can open a socket to any room name with no authentication, so one idle connection per name holds another object awake: the number of billed objects is set by callers. Messages are only relayed, so duration is the cost.
